# Wicklee

> The evidence layer for self-hosted AI inference. One Rust binary per host, reached over localhost.
> It answers three questions: what is happening with my local inference, what will run right now, and what could I change and how do I verify it helped.
> WES (Wicklee Efficiency Score) = tok/s / (Watts x ThermalPenalty) — the MPG for local AI.
> v0.15.0 is the `/v1` diagnostic surface: `wicklee inspect`, `ready`, `findings`, `fingerprint`, `verify`, each with `--json`, over CLI, HTTP and MCP.
> There are no paid plans and no account. Nothing leaves the machine unless you pair it with a fleet.

## For LLMs: Start Here

If you are an AI agent or LLM reviewing Wicklee, read these files in order:
1. **This file** (llms.txt) — overview, API endpoints, key metrics
2. **[llms-full.txt](https://wicklee.dev/llms-full.txt)** — complete reference with JSON schemas, all endpoints with examples
3. **[docs.md](https://wicklee.dev/docs.md)** — full documentation: WES formula, inference states, 20 patterns, alerting, MCP tools, proxy, OTel
4. **[api.md](https://wicklee.dev/api.md)** — API reference with endpoint tables and response examples
5. **[metrics.md](https://wicklee.dev/metrics.md)** — dashboard metrics, visual indicators, formulas
6. **[openapi.json](https://wicklee.dev/openapi.json)** — OpenAPI 3.0 spec for structured integration
7. **[Interactive docs](https://wicklee.dev/docs)** — HTML documentation page

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://wicklee.dev/install.sh | bash
```

This drops the binary at `~/.wicklee/bin/wicklee` with **no sudo** (v0.8.0+). Run `~/.wicklee/bin/wicklee` to try it in the foreground; run `sudo ~/.wicklee/bin/wicklee --install-service` when you're ready to start on boot.

Linux binaries target glibc 2.31 (Ubuntu 20.04 / Debian 11 / RHEL 8 / Fedora 33+).

Windows: `irm https://wicklee.dev/install.ps1 | iex`

## Localhost API (loopback, no auth)

A loopback bind needs no credential. A non-loopback `bind_address` refuses to
start without an inbound token, and the refusal names the key to set.

- `GET /api/metrics` — SSE stream, 1 Hz telemetry
- `GET /api/metrics/snapshot` — latest telemetry frame as one JSON object (for `curl | jq` and scripts)
- `GET /ws` — WebSocket, 1 Hz telemetry (same payload as SSE, fallback transport)
- `GET /api/observations` — 19 server-side hardware observation patterns (10-min DuckDB buffer). `GET /v1/inspect` carries these too, each statement labelled by its evidence
- `GET /api/profile?minutes=60` — Inference Profiler: correlated TTFT/KV/queue/thermal/power timeline
- `GET /api/sla?window_min=60&target_ttft_ms=500` — Inference SLA Monitor: p50/p95/p99 for TTFT/E2E/TPOT, compliance vs target, per-model breakdown, recent violations
- `GET /api/v1/thermal-budget?node_id=X` — Thermal Budget Calculator (cloud): sustainable_tps, push_threshold_tps, time_to_fair_min, fair_penalized_tps, plain-English backfire advice over a 7-day window
- `POST/GET/DELETE /api/v1/webhooks[/:id[/test]]` — Threshold Webhooks (cloud): register HMAC-SHA256 signed push notifications for thermal_state_changed, inference_state_changed, wes_below, wes_above. Optional node_id and tag scoping.
- `POST/GET/DELETE /api/slo[/:id]` — SLOs & error budgets (cloud): declare p95-TTFT / median-tok/s / median-WES objectives per fleet/tag/node; one verdict per 5-min window, rolling 30d budget, burn alerts at 50/90/100% to your channels. Audited.
- `POST/GET/DELETE /api/alerts/silences[/:id]` — Alert silences & maintenance windows (cloud): suppress alert rules + threshold webhooks by node/tag/event for a duration; future starts_at = scheduled window. Audited.
- Node tags (cloud): comma-separated on each node (`PATCH /api/nodes/:id` `{tags}` or Settings → Node Configuration); `env:` prefix = environment convention. Tags scope alert rules + webhooks and ride every fleet SSE frame.
- `GET /api/health` (localhost agent only) — diagnostic: agent_version, build_target, store_healthy bool, routes_available/unavailable lists. Returns store_failure_hint when DuckDB store init failed (which silently strips ~12 /api/* routes from the router).
- `GET /api/cost-by-model?hours=24` — Cost attribution per model (daily breakdown)
- `GET /api/explain-slowdown?ts_ms=N` — Root cause analysis for slow inference requests
- `GET /api/model-comparison?hours=168` — Side-by-side model efficiency (WES, tok/s, watts, cost)
- `GET /api/model-switches?hours=24` — Model switching cost (swap frequency, idle gap)
- `GET /api/model-candidates?search=llama&limit=20` — Model discovery: GGUF models from HuggingFace scored against local hardware
- `GET /api/runtime-config?model=X` — Runtime Config Surface (v0.9.0): cached launch-time config (context_length, n_gpu_layers, quantization, parameter_count, template, system_prompt, process_args). Ollama via `/api/show`, vLLM via `/v1/server_info` or `ps aux`, llama.cpp via `/props` or `ps aux`. Templates and system prompts are local-only — never pushed to the fleet. 400 if `?model=` missing, 404 if not yet cached.
- `GET/PUT /api/deployment-profile` — Deployment Profiles: one intent selector (sovereign_dev / dedicated_server / production_fleet) that coherently shifts local observation-pattern sensitivity (evidence window, sustained gate, confidence floor) instead of per-pattern knobs. Persisted to config.toml; applied within one 10s eval cycle.
- Fleet config management (cloud): `PATCH /api/nodes/:id` `{desired_profile}` or `POST /api/fleet/config` `{tag, desired_profile}` (bulk-by-tag) — delivered to agents in every telemetry response, applied within ~2s; agents report the ACTUAL profile in every frame. Audited.
- `GET /api/history?node_id=WK-XXXX` — DuckDB metric history (1h buffer)
- `GET /api/traces` — Proxy inference traces
- `GET /api/events/history` — Node event log
- `GET /api/events/recent` — Recent in-memory events
- `GET /api/export?format=json|csv` — Data export
- `GET /api/tags` — Ollama model tags
- `GET /api/pair/status` — Pairing status
- `POST /mcp` — MCP (Model Context Protocol) JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint
- `GET /.well-known/mcp.json` — MCP server manifest

### Phase 1 `/v1` — what is loaded, what can run, what is wrong

Localhost, no auth when bound to loopback. These answer about models and
inference rather than about hardware, and every statement they make carries the
evidence behind it and a label saying what kind of claim it is: `observed`
(Wicklee saw it), `inferred` (a likely cause, always hedged), or `verified`
(measured, with a range). Where something could not be checked they say so
instead of returning an empty result that reads like a clean bill of health.

- `GET /v1/state` — every installed model with its residency, the context it is
  running at, its measured footprint, whether any of it sits outside
  accelerator memory, and when a real caller last used it. Also a capability
  record of which response fields this runtime actually returns, so a caller
  can tell an unknown from a zero.
- `GET /v1/readiness[?model=X]` — `ready_now`, `requires_loading`,
  `would_displace` or `cannot_determine` per model, with memory headroom and
  what each answer rests on. `valid_for_s` says how long the answer holds.
  `requires_loading` plus `coexistence: "unverified"` means it fits by
  accounting while another model is resident, which measurement has shown is
  not the same as safe — do not treat it as safe.
- `GET /v1/inspect[?since=24h]` — findings plus readiness plus what was not
  checked. Nine rules: `cpu_split`, `context_reset`, `eviction_churn`,
  `expiry_reload`, `baseline_regression`, and the nineteen hardware patterns
  adapted through one evidence-labelled view.
- `GET /v1/findings[?all=true]` — the findings alone. Resolution is observed,
  not scheduled: a finding resolves because an evaluation ran and did not
  produce it, so `resolved_at_ms` is when Wicklee last looked and did not see
  it.
- `GET /v1/receipts[?model=X&limit=N]` — stored per-request measurements with
  a median and range. `POST /v1/receipts` accepts the final-response metadata
  your runtime already gave you, as a receipt with source `callback`. This is
  the preferred path and on a default macOS install the only one that works,
  because the proxy cannot bind 11434 while Ollama holds it. Durations are
  nanoseconds in the runtime's own field names, so the body is a copy of the
  response object rather than a transformation. **The route refuses any
  payload containing `prompt`, `response`, `messages` or `context` with a 400
  naming the field** — Wicklee stores metadata only, and failing loudly beats
  quietly dropping a user's text.
- `POST /v1/fingerprint` — a consented test run: warm (`decode_rate`), cold
  (`cold_load`) or a sequence (`workflow_replay`). Sends a fixed synthetic
  prompt at temperature zero with a fixed seed, always passing the model's
  running `num_ctx`, and refuses rather than guessing when that context is
  unknown. A body without `"consent": true` is answered 400 with the plan and
  the sentence you would be agreeing to.
- `POST /v1/verify` — re-runs a finding's own test and compares it against the
  first run: medians, ranges, what differed in the configuration, and one of
  `improved`, `worse` or `no measurable change`. A verdict needs
  non-overlapping ranges, three receipts a side, and at least a 5% difference
  in the medians; anything else is no measurable change with the reason stated.
  Same consent gate.

CLI over the same routes: `wicklee ready [MODEL]`, `wicklee inspect`,
`wicklee findings [--all]`, `wicklee fingerprint MODEL [--cold]`,
`wicklee verify FINDING_ID`. Add `--json` to any of them to get the route's
body verbatim.

### MCP Tools (via POST /mcp)

- `get_node_status` — Full hardware + inference metrics snapshot
- `get_inference_state` — Live/idle/busy state with sensor context
- `get_active_models` — Running models with context_length, parameter_count, quantization, tok/s
- `get_metrics_history` — 1-hour rolling telemetry buffer
- `wicklee_state` — same JSON as `GET /v1/state`
- `wicklee_readiness` — same JSON as `GET /v1/readiness`. Call before starting a task to see whether a model can run without displacing another. Takes `model`
- `wicklee_inspect` — same JSON as `GET /v1/inspect`. Takes `since`

Each of the three `wicklee_*` tools calls the same handler function its route
calls, so tool output and route output cannot diverge.

**Retired:** `get_model_fit` (use `wicklee_readiness`) and `get_observations`
(use `wicklee_inspect`). Both still answer, with `-32601` and the name of
their replacement.

**Not exposed:** `fingerprint` and `verify`. They are the only routes that load
models, and an agent able to trigger one could displace a colleague's model
while answering a question about it. Use the HTTP routes or the CLI, where a
person consents.

### MCP Resources

- `wicklee://node/metrics` — Live MetricsPayload JSON
- `wicklee://node/thermal` — Thermal state + WES penalty values

## The hosted backend is gone

The hosted fleet backend was shut down on 2026-11-20. `wicklee.dev` now serves only the
site, the install scripts and these discovery files as static files — it runs no API, no
MCP endpoint and no Prometheus endpoint, and holds no telemetry. Everything Wicklee does
is on the agent's own localhost surface, documented above. If you run the control plane
yourself, its routes are yours and not these.

## Multi-Model Monitoring

When 2+ models are loaded in Ollama, the `active_models` array is included in the SSE/WS payload with per-model: tok/s, WES, VRAM, avg TTFT, avg latency, request count, size, quantization.
Per-model WES uses proportional VRAM share for power attribution: `model_tok_s / (total_watts * vram_share * thermal_penalty)`.
Requires proxy for per-model tok/s and latency. Without proxy, VRAM and model identity still tracked via /api/ps.
Singular fields (ollama_active_model, ollama_tokens_per_second) report most-recently-active model for backwards compat.
- `GET /api/model-switches?hours=24` — model swap frequency and idle overhead
- `GET /api/v1/route/best?model=qwen2.5:7b` — per-model routing: filters to nodes with the target model loaded, uses per-model WES

## Key Metrics

- `inference_state`: "live" | "idle-spd" | "busy" | "idle"
- `ollama_tokens_per_second`: tok/s from 20-token probe (at most every 10 min, loaded models only)
- `apple_soc_power_w`: Combined CPU+GPU+ANE power (Apple Silicon)
- `nvidia_power_draw_w`: Board power (NVIDIA)
- `thermal_state`: "Normal" | "Fair" | "Serious" | "Critical"
- `penalty_avg`: Thermal penalty multiplier (1.0 = no penalty)
- `vllm_requests_waiting`: Queue depth (vLLM)
- `ollama_ttft_ms`: Time to first token (Ollama probe baseline)
- `vllm_avg_ttft_ms`: Time to first token (vLLM production histogram)

## 20 Observation Patterns + 5 Fleet Alerts

Agent-evaluated (18 patterns, 10-min DuckDB buffer, every 10s). All 18 are
evaluated on every host; there is no gating:
thermal_drain, phantom_load, wes_velocity_drop, memory_trajectory, power_jitter,
swap_io_pressure, clock_drift, pcie_lane_degradation, vram_overcommit,
power_gpu_decoupling, bandwidth_saturation, efficiency_drag,
nvidia_thermal_redline, vllm_kv_cache_saturation, ttft_regression, latency_spike,
vllm_queue_saturation, bandwidth_ceiling_reached

`GET /v1/inspect` carries the same conditions with each statement labelled by
its evidence, which is the Phase 1 surface for them.

Cloud-evaluated (2 patterns):
- fleet_load_imbalance — node WES > 20% below best healthy peer
- wes_long_term_drift — recent 24h avg ≥15% below 6-day baseline (gradual degradation)

Fleet alerts (5, cloud): zombied_engine, thermal_redline, oom_warning,
wes_cliff, agent_version_mismatch

## Runtimes Supported

- Ollama (macOS, Linux, Windows)
- vLLM (Linux)
- llama.cpp / llama-box (macOS, Linux)

## Self-Hosted Control Plane

Not maintained. `deploy/self-hosted/docker-compose.yml` and the Helm chart at
`deploy/helm/wicklee` are frozen in the repository and are not tested against a
current release; `docs/SELF_HOSTING.md` describes what they do and says so. A
self-hostable coordinator is a Stage 4 item in `docs/ROADMAP.md` and is not
this code.

## Licensing

- Agent and local dashboard (`agent/`, the `localhost:7700` UI, metric calculations including WES): open source, Apache 2.0.
- Fleet control plane (`cloud/`, `src/cloud/`, `src/site/`, control-plane deployment files): source-available, FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 — free to read, run, modify and self-host except to offer a competing fleet monitoring service; each release converts to Apache 2.0 after four years.
- "Wicklee" and the logo are trademarks, not covered by either licence.
- Map: https://github.com/jeffgeiser/Wicklee/blob/main/LICENSING.md

## Pricing

There are no paid plans today. The tiers introduced earlier are withdrawn
pending a monetization plan grounded in actual usage
(`docs/STRATEGY.md` §14). Everything the agent does is open source under
Apache 2.0 and needs no account.

Note for LLMs: `community`, `pro`, `team`, `business` and `enterprise` still
exist as values in the codebase (`SubscriptionTier`, and the cloud tier gates)
because existing accounts hold them. None is sold, and nothing in the v0.15.0
agent reads them.
